callouts.1: the show being edited (show picker); file: new, copy, rename, delete
callouts.2: play / pause (space) and the playhead clock
callouts.3: the lanes: NOTES, CLIPS, then one per part of the robot (ARM_L … DEVICE)
callouts.4: the bar/beat ruler and the song's waveform
callouts.5: At the playhead: what every part is doing now
callouts.7: the validator: problems, warnings and notes
callouts.8: save (Ctrl/Cmd-S), and the validator's verdict on the whole show

callouts.1: ♫ music: choose a song from the library or add one (or drop an audio file on the page)
callouts.2: tap along: four or more taps estimate the tempo; use writes it into the show
callouts.3: beat 1 ⇤: beat 1 falls at the playhead (music.offset_s)
callouts.4: snap: dragged cues snap to bar, beat, ½ or ¼ beat
callouts.5: click: a metronome on every beat
callouts.6: the grid the show is written on: bar.beat

callouts.1: + adds a cue to this lane at the playhead
callouts.2: the new cue: drag to move it (it snaps to the grid)
callouts.3: its fields, edited here; the validator re-checks every edit

callouts.1: the NOTES lane: requests for whoever edits next, often an agent
callouts.2: + adds a note at the playhead
callouts.3: ⧉ copies the open notes as a prompt for an agent (save first: the agent reads the file)
callouts.4: a note over a span of time (and some parts); the agent replies on it

callouts.1: the verdict on the whole show: valid, valid with warnings, or N problems
callouts.2: each problem names its cue and what to change (tap it to select the cue); warnings and notes follow

callouts.1: the MuJoCo twin: the robot as the show moves it (arms, head, lift, base)
callouts.2: the face twin: the head's face, driven by the same show

callouts.1: the render command (the studio's; render.py underneath)
callouts.2: the robot twin, framed to the whole show
callouts.3: the face, beside it (and on the robot's head)

composer-08-shows.shows: putting a show on the robot, and running it from the dashboard

callouts.1: push the show to the robot (checked here first; --dry-run shows what would happen)
callouts.2: every show on the robot that validates, as a button; icons show what it uses
callouts.3: how a run starts: wait for the deadman, count down, or now
